audit.primary_source_citation: DESIGNATED PRIMARY: Kopcow HD, Allan DSJ, Chen X, Rybalov B, Andzelm MM, Ge B, Strominger JL. "Human decidual NK cells form immature activating synapses and are not cytotoxic." Proc Natl Acad Sci USA 2005;102(43):15563-8. PMID 16230631, PMCID PMC1266146, doi 10.1073/pnas.0507835102. Full text retrieved and archived at /home/user/aaa/refs/R1_PMC1266146_fulltext.txt. — EARLIER IL-15 SOURCE (the one Kopcow cites as ref 15 for the rescue, "as described"): Verma S, Hiby SE, Loke YW, King A. Biol Reprod 2000;62(4):959-68, PMID 10727265, doi 10.1095/biolreprod62.4.959 — full text NOT retrievable, abstract+MeSH only. — ONLY IL-18 PRIMARY: Tokmadzic VS, Tsuji Y, Bogovic T, Laskarin G, Cupurdija K, Strbo N, Koyama K, Okamura H, Podack ER, Rukavina D. "IL-18 is present at the maternal-fetal interface and enhances cytotoxic activity of decidual lymphocytes." Am J Reprod Immunol 2002;48(4):191-200, PMID 12516629 — full text NOT retrievable, abstract only. NOTE: no single primary paper tests "IL-15/IL-18" as the claim states it; the compound is a review-level fusion (e.g. Le Bouteiller-adjacent review PMC3956423 cites Kopcow 2005 + El Costa 2008/2009 for that sentence, not an IL-15+IL-18 experiment).

audit.species: human (first-trimester decidua basalis from elective pregnancy terminations; peripheral blood NK from adult donors as comparator). No animal work anywhere in the load-bearing source.
audit.what_was_measured: In humans, dNK were isolated from first-trimester decidua basalis obtained at elective abortion (gestational age never stated in the paper), enriched by immunomagnetic depletion of CD3+ and CD16+ cells and further purified with anti-CD56 beads; at the fresh timepoint (t=0, immediately after tissue digestion and bead purification) and after 36 h of culture in 12 ng/ml IL-15 in RPMI-1640 + 10% FCS, specific lysis of 51Cr-labelled 721.221 and K562 target cells was measured in 4-h chromium-release assays across graded E:T ratios, against autologous-preparation fresh dNK and against peripheral-blood NK; in parallel, at 20 min of conjugation, the percentage of dNK-721.221 conjugates showing MTOC (alpha/gamma-tubulin) and perforin-granule polarization toward the contact site, and the percentage showing CD2 / LFA-1 / F-actin accumulation at the contact site, were scored by confocal microscopy on at least 50 conjugates per slide. n = 4 independent decidual preparations for the fresh dNK vs pNK lysis comparison, n = 3 for the 36-h IL-15 arm (one shown as representative), and at least 3 for every polarization percentage. Readouts: % specific 51Cr release; % conjugates with polarized MTOC/perforin (fresh dNK 19%, IL-15-cultured dNK 66%, pNK 55%, YTS 74%).
audit.n: 3 (IL-15 rescue arm, the load-bearing experiment); 4 (fresh dNK vs pNK lysis); >=3 (each polarization percentage). Counter-source Siewiera 2013: 10.
audit.n_unit: independent decidual preparations, each from a separate first-trimester elective termination (the paper says only "independent experiments" and never states a donor count, gestational age, or purity figure; unit inferred from "dNK from the same preparation"). Siewiera's n = 10 is stated as "a cohort of 10 decidua basalis", i.e. donors. NOT cells: the confocal ">=50 conjugates per slide" and "n >= 70 perforin-positive cells per slide" figures are cell counts and are NOT the n.
audit.controls: PRESENT in Kopcow 2005: peripheral-blood NK as a cytotoxic positive control on the same targets; a mock-isolation control in which pNK were run through the dNK isolation procedure (ruled out the isolation protocol as the cause of low fresh-dNK killing); paired design for the rescue (fresh dNK vs "dNK from the same preparation" cultured with IL-15); IgG isotype controls for receptor FACS; MHC-I-negative targets (721.221, K562) plus 721.221/HLA-G transfectants and BeWo/JEG3 trophoblast lines to test HLA-G/class-I dependence; resting (unconjugated) NK controls for granule clustering; YTS cell line as a second cytotoxic reference. MISSING, and material to the claim: (1) no 36-h medium-only / no-cytokine culture arm — the comparison is fresh (t=0) vs 36 h + IL-15, so time in culture and removal from decidual tissue are fully confounded with the cytokine; (2) no IL-15 dose-response and no anti-IL-15 or IL-15Ra blockade; (3) no post-culture purity, viability, count or division tracking, so preferential survival/outgrowth of a minority already-competent cell is not excluded; (4) IL-18 was never tested by Kopcow at all; (5) no donor-level statistics (representative experiment shown for the rescue).
audit.strongest_alternative_explanation: The 36-h ex vivo culture, not IL-15, does the work — and the paper itself offers this. Kopcow's own Discussion states the alternative verbatim: "the immunosuppressive environment of the decidua might be responsible for blocking MTOC and granule polarization. Regain of cytotoxicity may result from the removal of dNK from this environment, for example, by in vitro incubation in the presence of IL-15." Because there is no 36-h medium-only arm, nothing in the data separates "IL-15 signals a state change" from "release from tissue-imposed suppression plus 36 h of recovery from collagenase digestion and bead handling". Second, non-exclusive alternative: selection rather than conversion — IL-15 is a survival/proliferation factor for CD56bright NK, no purity, count, viability or division tracking was done after culture, and the starting population is only bead-enriched (CD3/CD16 depletion does not exclude a CD16-neg-but-competent or contaminating minority), so preferential survival/expansion of an already-cytotoxic minority reproduces both the lysis curve and the 19%->66% polarization shift without any single cell changing state. Third (G4, mechanism's home field): the entire phenotype is generic to freshly isolated tissue lymphocytes, not specific to decidual identity — CD8+ tumour-infiltrating T cells are nonlytic immediately on isolation despite full perforin/granzyme granule content, with the same defect in MTOC mobilization and lytic granule exocytosis (Radoja/Frey, PMID 11673513, cited by Kopcow as ref 27), and TIL effector function is likewise restored by ex vivo gamma-c cytokine culture (e.g. IL-2, PMC2377057). A result that reproduces in TILs, CD8 T cells and dNK alike is evidence about ex vivo culture of tissue lymphocytes, not about a dNK-specific licensing switch. Fourth, the baseline is not zero: fresh dNK already lysed at ~15% of pNK levels and already polarized granules in 19-22% of conjugates, so the effect is a quantitative increase from a non-zero baseline, not the flipping of an off switch.
audit.counter_evidence: FOUND — four independent lines. (1) DIRECT CONTRADICTION OF THE CLAIM'S OWN CYTOKINE PAIR: Tokmadzic 2002 (PMID 12516629), the only primary study that actually tested IL-18 on decidual cells, reports that in decidual lymphocytes from 6-10 wk terminations, IL-18 at 10 ng/ml up-regulated perforin and cytolytic activity and "simultaneous stimulation with IL-18 and IL-12 enhanced DL cytolytic activity, while IL-18 combined with IL-10 or IL-15 did not show this effect." The specific IL-15+IL-18 combination named in the claim is the one combination reported NOT to work; the working partner for IL-18 was IL-12. (Abstract only — see fulltext field.) Note also its readout was bulk decidual lymphocytes, not purified dNK. (2) NO CYTOKINE IS REQUIRED AT ALL: El Costa 2008 (PMID 18713971) reports that in FRESH, uncultured dNK, mAb engagement of NKp46 (and to a lesser extent NKG2C, but not NKp30) induced calcium mobilization, perforin polarization, granule exocytosis and efficient target lysis — no IL-15, no IL-18, no culture period. (Abstract only.) (3) Siewiera 2013 (PMID 23592985, PMC3617138, FULL TEXT READ): fresh dNK purified from 8-12 wk decidua basalis killed autologous HCMV-infected decidual fibroblasts in 18-h 51Cr assays, reaching ~75% specific lysis at E:T 50 with no killing of uninfected autologous fibroblasts, confirmed across "a cohort of 10 decidua basalis"; 83+/-4% of dNK synapses with infected targets showed polarized perforin granules vs 28% with uninfected targets, and CD107a degranulation rose from 6 h. No exogenous IL-15/IL-18 was added. Cytotoxicity is gated by target-derived activating ligand, not licensed by these two cytokines. (4) THE "RELEASE DEFECT" FRAMING IS ITSELF CONTESTED: Vujaklija 2011 (PMID 21623991) reports >85% of first-trimester decidual CD56+ cells contain granulysin and "when cultured spontaneously release high quantities of GNLY" (ELISA on purified NK) — i.e. secretion is not globally blocked; and Crespo 2020 Cell (PMID 32822574) shows fresh human dNK selectively transfer granulysin through nanotubes into extravillous trophoblasts to kill intracellular Listeria without killing the trophoblast. Fresh dNK therefore have an intact, directed granule-delivery route; what is restrained is host-cell lysis specifically. Searched and NOT found: any study reporting failure of IL-15 to increase dNK killing, and any in vivo (human or mouse) test of IL-15/IL-18-restored uNK cytotoxicity — recorded as searched-and-nothing-read, not as absence.
audit.downstream_dependency: Named, concrete: (a) Phase B gate B1 as pre-registered in docs/PREREGISTRATION.md §3 — "A claim of the form 'A becomes functionally B-like' is not decidable — lineage does not measure function." Because R1 is exactly that form, R1's audit result is the sole determinant of whether R1 enters Phase B/C or is routed out; it also fails shortlist criterion 3 of §5 for the same reason. Note R1 fails §5 criterion 1 as well at MEDIUM. (b) The state-vs-lineage framing that three other rows in phaseA/claims.json lean on: T3 (peripheral blood NK -> decidual NK-like, Keskin 2007 / Cerdeira 2013, in vitro only), T5 (glycodelin-A -> dNK-like, in vitro) and X3 (tumour NK -> decidual-like/pro-angiogenic). If the decidual program is a reversible, environment-imposed functional state that a cytokine can toggle back within 36 h, then the forward in vitro conversions in T3/T5/X3 are state-switching in a two-way-reversible system and carry no ancestry content; if instead dNK hypofunction were a fixed differentiation endpoint, those forward conversions would be the more interesting lineage read. R1 is the row that supplies the reverse direction of that argument. It is MEDIUM rather than HIGH because no lineage conclusion anywhere in the registry is derived from R1 being true — deleting R1 changes the framing of T3/T5/X3 but overturns no ancestry claim — and rather than LOW because it is the only row carrying the reverse-direction evidence.
audit.audit_overturns_detail: The initial call "FUNCTIONAL, NOT LINEAGE" survives the audit intact and is confirmed by the methods: not one experiment in Kopcow 2005, Verma 2000, Tokmadzic 2002, El Costa 2008 or Siewiera 2013 follows a cell to a descendant, transfers a population, marks a clone, or otherwise asserts ancestry. Nothing is overturned about the CALL. What the audit does change is the CLAIM's own wording, which is more specific than any primary source supports: (i) "IL-15/IL-18" is a compound that no single primary paper tested — the pairing appears to be a review-level fusion (the review at PMC3956423 that carries the "IL-15 and IL-18" sentence cites Kopcow 2005 and El Costa 2008/2009, none of which used IL-18); (ii) the one primary study that did test that exact pair reports it did NOT work (Tokmadzic 2002: IL-18 + IL-15 gave no enhancement, IL-18 + IL-12 did), and it used bulk decidual lymphocytes, not purified dNK; (iii) the IL-15 half rests on a 3-preparation, single-representative-figure experiment with no 36-h no-cytokine control arm, so "IL-15 rescue" is not separable from "36 h out of the decidua"; (iv) "made cytotoxic" overstates a baseline that was already ~15% of pNK lysis with 19-22% granule polarization. Also recorded against the hint supplied with the task: the "granules present but not released" framing is correct as far as Kopcow goes (granzyme A/B and perforin are abundant; CD2, LFA-1 and F-actin polarize normally; MTOC and perforin granules do not), i.e. a synapse-maturation/polarization defect rather than a differentiation deficit — but that framing is itself only partly right, since fresh dNK do polarize and exocytose when NKp46 is crosslinked (El Costa 2008), when the target is HCMV-infected (Siewiera 2013), and they spontaneously secrete granulysin and nanotube-deliver it into trophoblasts (Vujaklija 2011; Crespo 2020). The defect is conditional and target-gated, not constitutive.
audit.methods_quote: Kopcow 2005 Methods, verbatim: "dNK cells were isolated from decidua basalis obtained from patients undergoing first-trimester elective abortions as described (14), except that dNK enrichment was achieved by depletion of CD3+ cells and CD16+ cells with immuno-magnetic beads (Miltenyi Biotech). dNK were then used for confocal microscopy or were further purified with anti-CD56 coated magnetic beads for cytotoxicity experiments or for culture in the presence of 12 ng/ml IL-15 (PeproTech)." / "The cytotoxic activity of dNK, pNK, or IL-15-treated dNK on 721.221 or K562 cells was assessed by 4-h 51Cr-release assays (24)." / "Accumulation of molecules at the NKIS and perforin and MTOC polarization were calculated from at least 50 conjugates per slide... All percentages presented are the average of at least three independent experiments." Results/legend, verbatim: "dNK cytotoxic capacity was regained upon incubation of the cells with IL-15 for 12 h (data not shown) or 36 h (Fig. 1B) as described (15)." / Fig. 1B legend: "Cytotoxic activity of dNK (filled squares) and dNK from the same preparation incubated for 36 h with IL-15 (12 ng/ml) in RPMI medium 1640 plus 10% FCS (open squares) on 721.221 targets (one representative experiment of three)." / "The gain of cytolytic capacity upon stimulation of dNK with IL-15 (Fig. 1B) was paralleled by an increase in the percentage of conjugates with polarized MTOC and perforin-containing granules to 66% in IL-15 stimulated dNK cells conjugated with 721.221 (Fig. 5)." / Discussion, the authors' own confound: "Alternatively, the immunosuppressive environment of the decidua might be responsible for blocking MTOC and granule polarization. Regain of cytotoxicity may result from the removal of dNK from this environment, for example, by in vitro incubation in the presence of IL-15."
audit.notes: IS THIS A LINEAGE CLAIM? No. Stated plainly as the task requires: R1 is a FUNCTIONAL claim ("can dNK's cytotoxic function be switched on"), not an ancestry claim ("does A give rise to B"). Every experiment behind it measures an effector readout — % specific 51Cr release, % conjugates with polarized MTOC/perforin, CD107a surface exposure, perforin/granulysin content — on a population of cells at two timepoints. No clone, barcode, congenic marker, transfer, fate map or genetic recorder appears anywhere in the load-bearing literature. The cells before and after IL-15 are not shown to be the same cells; that identity is assumed, not measured, which is precisely the gap a lineage method would fill but which no cited study attempts. The one place ancestry language creeps in is Siewiera 2013's observation that after 48 h of contact with HCMV-infected autologous fibroblasts the dNK CD56bright fraction fell from 76.3+/-5% to 48+/-6.3% while CD56dim rose to 40+/-4% with CD16 acquisition in 41% (vs 4.3%) — a phenotype shift that touches claim D3 (CD56bright -> CD56dim), but Siewiera measure it as bulk population percentages in coculture and explicitly cannot distinguish conversion from selective survival/expansion; it is not offered as, and does not constitute, lineage evidence. CLASSIFICATION RATIONALE (G7, no loosening): strongest = INF_INVITRO because the load-bearing experiment is "cells cultured into a phenotype in vitro" exactly as the §2 taxonomy defines it; INF_MARKER is also present because much of the argument's force comes from static content markers (perforin, granzyme A/B, NKp30/44/46, NKG2D, 2B4, LFA-1 present at pNK-equal or higher levels => "loaded to kill"). No OBS_DIRECT, OBS_TRANSFER or OBS_GENETIC evidence exists for this claim in any species; there is no in vivo test of the rescue at all. INF_TRAJECTORY does not arise (no pseudotime/velocity anywhere), and INF_KINETIC was considered and rejected — the 12 h vs 36 h timing is an internal feature of the same in vitro experiment, not an "A appears before B in time" argument. ARCHIVED under refs/ with tag R1: R1_PMC1266146_fulltext.txt (Kopcow, full, scraped from PMC), R1_PMC1266146.txt, R1_PMC3617138.txt (Siewiera, OA full), R1_10727265.txt (Verma, abstract), R1_12516629.txt (Tokmadzic, abstract), R1_18713971.txt (El Costa, abstract), R1_21623991.txt (Vujaklija, abstract), R1_PMC7484179.txt (Crespo, abstract), R1_PMC5301153.txt (Zhang 2017, abstract). NOT SEARCHED (recorded as such per G3, not as absent): mtDNA/mtscATAC/MAESTER/barcode occupancy for dNK (that is Phase B gate B4, out of scope for this row); mouse uNK IL-15/IL-18 cytotoxicity restoration in vivo was queried once ("IL-15 uterine NK cells mouse") and returned nothing on point, so it is searched-and-nothing-read rather than absent.

adv.challenge_reason:
Strongest class stays INF_INVITRO — I re-derived it from Kopcow 2005 full text myself (/home/user/aaa/refs/R1_PMC1266146_fulltext.txt), not from the prior row. No OBS_* exists: nothing follows a cell, transfers a population, marks a clone, or knocks out a gene. Three substantive corrections to the prior row, none of which loosen anything (G7):

(1) THE PROMPT'S SPECIFIC TRAP IS PRESENT AND WAS NOT FLAGGED. Kopcow's headline deficit ("dNK lyse at ~15% of pNK") and its restoration endpoint ("IL-15 dNK 66% MTOC/perforin polarization vs pNK 55%") are BETWEEN-INDIVIDUAL population comparisons. Methods state dNK come from first-trimester termination patients and pNK "were isolated from peripheral blood as described (14)" — the paper never states the blood was autologous or donor-matched, and no pairing appears in any figure legend. So both the deficit and the claimed "restoration to peripheral-like" rest on comparing cells from different people. That is INF_MARKER, not observation. The prior row listed INF_MARKER but grounded it only in "static content markers (perforin, granzyme A/B, NKp30/44/46)"; the cross-individual comparison is the stronger and previously unstated reason.

(2) INF_KINETIC IS PRESENT AND WAS WRONGLY REJECTED. The prior row rejected it because "the 12 h vs 36 h timing is internal to the same in vitro experiment." That misreads the taxonomy. The load-bearing inference is that the cells that lysed at 36 h ARE the cells that failed to lyse at t=0. The only support for that is temporal ordering of two bulk population snapshots sharing the label "same preparation" (Fig 1B: "dNK (filled squares) and dNK from the same preparation incubated for 36 h with IL-15"). No cell identity is tracked between the snapshots. "State A at t=0, state B at t=36 h, therefore A became B" is exactly §2's INF_KINETIC. Revised evidence_types_all = [INF_INVITRO, INF_MARKER, INF_KINETIC]. INF_TRAJECTORY correctly absent (no pseudotime/velocity anywhere).

(3) THE n_unit IS OVER-SPECIFIED AND VOIDS UNDER G5 AS WRITTEN. The prior row states n_unit = "independent decidual preparations, each from a separate first-trimester elective termination." The phrase "each from a separate termination" appears nowhere in Kopcow. The paper says only "the average of at least three independent experiments" (Methods), "average of four independent experiments" (Fig 1A), "one representative experiment of three" (Fig 1B). It never states a donor count, gestational age, purity, viability or post-culture cell number. "Independent experiment" is not shown to equal "one donor" — the cited isolation protocol (Koopman 2003, ref 14) is not reproduced, and pooling across deciduas is neither excluded nor mentioned. Correct entry per G5: n = 3 (IL-15 rescue arm), 4 (fresh dNK vs pNK), >=3 (each polarization percentage); n_unit = "independent experiments; donor count NOT STATED in the source." The >=50 conjugates/slide and >=70 perforin-positive cells/slide are cell counts and are correctly excluded as n.

Everything else in the prior row's methods reading checks out against the text: 12 ng/ml IL-15, 36 h in RPMI-1640 + 10% FCS, 4-h 51Cr release on 721.221/K562, confocal MTOC/perforin scoring, and the missing controls (no 36-h medium-only arm, no IL-15 dose-response, no anti-IL-15 blockade, no post-culture purity/count/division tracking, IL-18 never tested by Kopcow). The paper's own Discussion states the confound verbatim.
adv.new_counter_evidence:
SEVEN lines the prior auditor missed. Ranked by force.

(1) THE CLAIM'S OWN CYTOKINE IS ABUNDANT IN VIVO — INTERNAL CONTRADICTION, AND IT WAS SITTING IN THE PRIOR ROW'S OWN ARCHIVE. Kitaya 2000 (PMID 10952908, Biol Reprod, abstract only): IL-15 mRNA and protein are elevated in first-trimester decidua — stromal and perivascular cells, endothelium — with MEMBRANE-BOUND IL-15 detected on first-trimester decidual cells by flow, progesterone-inducible. Verma 2000's own abstract (PMID 10727265, archived by the prior auditor as R1_10727265.txt): "Both IL-15 mRNA and protein were found in a variety of cells but particularly in decidual macrophages." dNK are therefore already bathed in IL-15, including membrane-presented IL-15, in situ — and are non-cytotoxic there. Adding IL-15 in vitro cannot be the differential variable. This converts Kopcow's own stated alternative ("Regain of cytotoxicity may result from the removal of dNK from this environment") from a possibility into the better-supported reading, and it is a stronger argument than the prior row's "no medium-only arm" point because it does not depend on a missing control.

(2) IL-15's DOCUMENTED IN VIVO ROLE IN THE UTERUS IS POPULATION DEVELOPMENT, NOT ACUTE LICENSING — AND THE PRIOR ROW RECORDED THIS AS "SEARCHED, NOTHING FOUND" (a search failure, not an absence, per G3). Barber & Pollard 2003 (PMID 12816981, J Immunol, mouse, abstract only): IL-15-/- mice have NO mature or immature uNK cells; Rag2-/-gc-/- bone-marrow transplant shows uNK derive from BM and REQUIRE IL-15 to develop. Ashkar 2003 (PMID 12960317, J Immunol, mouse, abstract only): IL-15-/- implantation sites contain no uNK, no spiral-artery modification; and critically, "Terminal differentiation of uNK cells was not promoted in pregnant IRF-1(-/-) mice by 5-day infusion of murine rIL-15" — an actual in vivo rIL-15 infusion, negative on the maturation readout. So the one animal system where IL-15 has been manipulated in the uterus shows IL-15 governs whether uNK EXIST, which is precisely the survival/outgrowth confound Kopcow left uncontrolled (no post-culture count, viability, purity or division tracking over 36 h).

(3) THE SAME MANIPULATION IS CREDITED WITH THE OPPOSITE DESTINATION. Manaster 2008 (PMID 18641324, J Immunol, abstract only): endometrial NK "lack NK-specific functional phenotype and activity such as cytokine secretion and cytotoxicity, before IL-15 stimulation. Following such stimulation, endometrial NK cells acquire phenotype and function that are similar to those of DECIDUAL NK cells." In R1, IL-15 culture of uterine-lineage NK is evidence they become pNK-like/cytotoxic; in Manaster, IL-15 culture of uterine-lineage NK is evidence they become dNK-like. IL-15 culture is a generic activation manipulation whose "destination phenotype" is assigned by whichever endpoint the authors chose to measure. This is a direct internal-consistency counter and it also lands on registry rows T3 and T5.

(4) FRESH dNK CYTOTOXICITY IS GESTATIONAL-AGE-DEPENDENT, WITH NO CYTOKINE ADDED — FROM KOPCOW'S OWN LAB. de Mendonca Vieira 2020 (PMID 32376646, PMC7322730, J Immunol, Strominger/Tilburgs, abstract only): term-pregnancy dNK from decidua basalis and parietalis have "an increased degranulation response to K562 and PMA/ionomycin" versus first-trimester dNK and pNK, but lower capacity against HCMV-infected cells. No IL-15, no IL-18. NOTE, per the prompt's challenge item: this too is a population comparison across DIFFERENT individuals (term donors vs first-trimester donors vs blood donors) and cannot show that first-trimester dNK became term dNK — INF_MARKER at best, and I am not crediting it as anything more.

(5) A 2026 OA PAPER WITH DONOR-MATCHED COMPARTMENTS SHOWS THE CLAIM'S CYTOKINES FAILING. PMID 41808348 / PMC12975338 (Immunohorizons 2026; FULL TEXT READ, archived R1_PMC12975338.txt). Methods verbatim: "Cells were isolated from tissues or blood as described above. Directly after isolation (without cryopreservation), 500,000 cells were placed into each well of a U-bottom 96-well plate with 200 ul complete media. Cells were then stimulated with IL-12, IL-15 and IL-18 (each at 1 nM) for 24hrs. GolgiPlug was added after 20hrs of culture." Bulk RNA-seq n = 6 maternal blood / 8 decidual-placental interface (DPI) / 6 decidua, from 6 MATCHED donors plus 2 additional DPI donors. Result: "a significant and striking lack in the ability of NK cells isolated from the decidual-placental interface (DPI) to produce interferon-g in response to the activating cytokines IL-12, IL-15, and IL-18. In contrast, NK cells from the decidua retained their responsiveness." Exogenous IL-15+IL-18 therefore does NOT restore effector function across the maternal-fetal interface; rescuability is compartment-specific. Honest caveat, stated because the row must not overclaim: the readout is IFN-gamma, not lysis, the tissue is term, and the decidua-proper arm is CONSISTENT with rescue. This is the only donor-matched-compartment design in the whole R1 literature.

(6) THE "NOT CYTOTOXIC" PREMISE WAS ALREADY CONTESTED BY THE TWO PAPERS KOPCOW HIMSELF CITES AS CONFLICTING (refs 16, 17) — neither appears in the prior row. Deniz 1994 (PMID 8157952, J Immunol, abstract only): CD3- decidual granulated leukocyte CLONES "showed MHC-nonrestricted NK cell activity"; "Class I HLA Ag loss cell mutants were killed efficiently by CD3- DGL clones." Ponte 1999 (PMID 10318943, PNAS, abstract only): HLA-G1-transfected 221 "was fully protected from decidual NK cells" — which entails untransfected 221 was lysed by them. Cloning is literally selection plus expansion, so this is the cleanest existing demonstration that cytotoxic dNK are recoverable by outgrowth of a subset rather than by state conversion of the bulk — the alternative Kopcow cannot exclude.

(7) THE PRIOR ROW'S FLAT CLAIM THAT "NO SINGLE PRIMARY PAPER TESTS IL-15/IL-18" IS PROBABLY WRONG. PubMed's MeSH record for Verma 2000 — the very paper Kopcow cites as ref 15 "as described" for the rescue — carries substance terms Interleukin-15, Interleukin-18 AND Interleukin-12, with qualifier headings "Interleukin-12 biosynthesis pharmacology" and "Interleukin-18 pharmacology". The pharmacology qualifier is assigned from full text and indicates the agents were administered in that study; the abstract is silent on both. So the "IL-15/IL-18" pairing may originate in Verma 2000 itself rather than being the "review-level fusion" the prior row asserted. Recorded strictly as an INDEXING-LEVEL LEAD, not a finding: the full text is unobtainable (see better_primary_source), so under G1 no methods-derived statement may be built on it. It does, however, remove the prior row's confident negative.

CONFIRMED FROM THE PRIOR ROW (I re-read the archived sources): Tokmadzic 2002 (PMID 12516629) does report "IL-18 combined with IL-10 or IL-15 did not show this effect," i.e. the exact pair named in the claim is the one reported not to work, with IL-12 as the working partner — and its readout is bulk decidual lymphocytes, not purified dNK. Siewiera 2013, El Costa 2008, Vujaklija 2011 and Crespo 2020 stand as reported.

SEARCHED AND NOTHING ON POINT READ (not "absent"): no study repeating Kopcow's IL-15 rescue with a 36-h medium-only control arm; no study reporting failure of IL-15 to raise dNK lysis specifically; no in vivo test of cytokine-restored uNK CYTOTOXICITY in any species. NOT_SEARCHED, recorded per G3: ILC1/ILC3 plasticity literature on cytokine-driven functional reversal; human NK exhaustion in chronic HIV/HCV and whether IL-15 restores killing there; mtDNA/mtscATAC/MAESTER/barcode occupancy for dNK (Phase B4, out of scope for this row).
adv.crossfield_g4_findings:
The mechanism's home field does not merely fail to support R1 — it says the specific readout R1 asserts is the one that does NOT durably change, and that R1's experimental design cannot distinguish reprogramming from acute activation.

A. NK'S OWN HOME FIELD FOR THIS EXACT MANIPULATION IS CYTOKINE-INDUCED MEMORY-LIKE (CIML) NK, AND ITS RESULT CUTS AGAINST R1. Cooper 2009 (PMID 19181844, PNAS, mouse, abstract only): NK preactivated with IL-12/IL-15/IL-18 were adoptively transferred into naive hosts and congenically re-identified 7-22 days later. They "produce significantly more IFN-gamma when restimulated. This memory-like property is intrinsic to the NK cell. By contrast, memory-like NK cells DO NOT EXPRESS GRANZYME B PROTEIN AND KILL TARGETS SIMILARLY TO NAIVE NK CELLS." This is an OBS_TRANSFER-grade in vivo test of a cytokine-induced NK functional state change, and it separates the two readouts cleanly: IFN-gamma persists, cytotoxicity does not. Romee 2016 (PMID 27655849, Sci Transl Med, human, abstract only) establishes the design standard: "differentiate after a brief preactivation with IL-12, IL-15, and IL-18 and exhibit enhanced responses to cytokine or activating receptor RESTIMULATION for WEEKS TO MONTHS AFTER preactivation." Two consequences for R1: (i) the replicated cocktail is IL-12+IL-15+IL-18, so the claim's bare "IL-15/IL-18" is plausibly a garbled CIML protocol — and Tokmadzic 2002 independently found IL-12, not IL-15, to be IL-18's working partner on decidual lymphocytes; (ii) Kopcow measured dNK at the end of 36 h of CONTINUOUS IL-15 exposure with no washout, no rest and no re-challenge, so his result is by construction an acute-activation measurement, not a demonstration that any state changed.

B. THE uNK FIELD'S OWN TRAINED-IMMUNITY RESULT AGREES, AND IT IS ALREADY IN THIS REGISTRY AS R4. Gamliel 2018 (PMID 29768178, Immunity, abstract only): Pregnancy-Trained decidual NK from repeated pregnancies carry "a unique transcriptome and epigenetic signature" with "open chromatin around the enhancers of IFNG and VEGFA," and activation yields increased IFN-gamma and VEGF-alpha. The epigenetically encoded, persisting uNK program is cytokine/growth-factor secretion. Cytotoxicity is again not the trained axis.

C. T-CELL EXHAUSTION: FUNCTIONAL RESCUE MEASURED UNDER CONTINUING STIMULUS IS THE FIELD'S CANONICAL FALSE POSITIVE. Pauken 2016 (PMID 27789795, Science, mouse, abstract only): PD-L1 blockade reinvigorates exhausted CD8 T cells transcriptionally, but their epigenetic profile "was minimally remodeled after PD-L1 blockade"; reinvigorated cells "became reexhausted if antigen concentration remained high and failed to become T MEM upon antigen clearance" — "epigenetic fate inflexibility may limit current immunotherapies." Sen 2016 (PMID 27789799, Science) maps the exhaustion-specific enhancer landscape. Philip 2017 (PMID 28514453, Nature; OA, methods section retrieved but empty of body text — treated as abstract-level) establishes two chromatin states, an early plastic/reprogrammable one and a late FIXED one that resists reprogramming. Ghoneim 2017 (PMID 28648661, Cell) shows de novo DNA methylation restricts PD-1-blockade rejuvenation. Khan 2019 (PMID 31207603, Nature) identifies TOX as the transcriptional/epigenetic programmer. The field's operating standard is therefore: withdraw the stimulus, rest, re-challenge, and profile chromatin or methylation. Kopcow did none of the three. Under that standard his 19%->66% polarization shift and lysis-curve rise are uninformative about whether the decidual program was altered at all.

D. TRAINED IMMUNITY: DURABLE INNATE REPROGRAMMING IS DEMONSTRATED BY SURVIVING WITHDRAWAL, AND IT IS STORED IN PROGENITORS, NOT IN THE MATURE EFFECTOR. Saeed 2014 (PMID 25258085, Science): beta-glucan epigenetically programs monocyte-to-macrophage differentiation. Kaufmann 2018 (PMID 29328912, Cell): BCG educates hematopoietic stem cells. Cirovic 2020 (PMID 32544459, Cell Host Microbe; OA, STAR Methods retrieved): BCG in humans elicits trained immunity via the hematopoietic PROGENITOR compartment. Bearing on R1: mature dNK held 36 h in continuously present IL-15, never washed out, never re-challenged, with no progenitor compartment sampled, satisfies no criterion this field uses. Nothing in Kopcow distinguishes "reprogrammed" from "activated while the cytokine is still in the well."

E. TGF-BETA IMPRINTING — SEARCHED, NOTHING RETRIEVED. Two lit.py queries ("TGF-beta imprinting tissue residency CD8 T cells epigenetic"; "NK cell exhaustion TGF-beta epigenetic imprinting reversibility") returned zero PubMed hits. Recorded as searched-and-nothing-read, NOT as absent (G3). This matters because registry row R3 asserts the opposite polarity for the same object (after TGF-beta withdrawal residency reverts but effector function does not); the cross-field evidence for that polarity was not obtained here and R3 must supply it itself.

NET G4 VERDICT: across three independent fields — CIML NK, T-cell exhaustion, monocyte trained immunity — every system in which a durable cytokine-induced functional state change has actually been demonstrated used stimulus withdrawal plus re-challenge, and in the one that used adoptive transfer (Cooper 2009) the durable readout was IFN-gamma while KILLING RETURNED TO BASELINE. R1 asserts the single readout the home field reports as non-durable, on the single design the home field treats as unable to detect durability.

adv.load_bearing_reason:
MEDIUM -> LOW. I checked the repo rather than reasoning about it. `grep -rn '\bR1\b'` across every .py/.js/.md/.json in /home/user/aaa returns exactly three hits: phaseA/claims.json:23 (the claim's own row), docs/PREREGISTRATION.md:20 (the §1 scope enumeration "D1-D4, P1-P3, T1-T6, S1-S3, X1-X5, R1-R4"), and docs/DECISIONS.md:11 (the arithmetic that totals 25 claims). Nothing derives a conclusion from R1 being true.

THE PRIOR ROW'S FIRST DEPENDENCY IS CIRCULAR. It names "Phase B gate B1 ... R1's audit result is the sole determinant of whether R1 enters Phase B/C." A row determining its own routing is not a downstream dependency. Worse, it is not even true: I read scripts/phaseB_workflow.js, and B1 is applied to the CLAIM TEXT, not to the audit — its rule table is literally "'A becomes functionally B-like' -> NOT DECIDABLE (lineage does not measure function)". R1's text is "dNK -> cytotoxic (IL-15/IL-18 rescue)". B1 returns FALSE from the claim's grammatical form alone. Every finding in this audit could be reversed and B1's answer would not move.

THE PRIOR ROW'S SECOND DEPENDENCY IS NOT A COMPUTED INPUT. It claims T3, T5 and X3 "lean on" R1's state-vs-lineage framing. I read scripts/build_tables.py: T1 rows are built per-claim from that claim's own audit/adv record (`merged_evidence`, `merged_load_bearing`, `merged_counter`), and Phase B eligibility is computed as `merged_evidence(recs[c])[0] in INF` per claim. No field of T3, T5 or X3 reads any field of R1. Each is graded on its own primaries (Keskin 2007 / Cerdeira 2013; glycodelin-A; tumour NK). Deleting R1 changes none of their classifications, none of their B1/B2 answers, and none of their shortlist status. What the prior row called a dependency is a narrative connection — and §7 explicitly forbids opining on scientific value, which is the register that argument sits in.

WHAT ACTUALLY CHANGES IF R1 IS DELETED: one line of results/T1_evidence_audit.tsv, and the claim count in docs/DECISIONS.md drops from 25 to 24. That is the whole blast radius.

WHY NOT LOWER THAN LOW: LOW is the floor, and R1 does still occupy a real slot — it is the only row carrying the reverse-direction (restoration) evidence in the `reversal` group, and it is in tension with R3 ("after TGF-beta withdrawal residency reverts, effector function does not"), which asserts the opposite polarity about tissue-NK effector function. But that tension is between two independently sourced rows; R3's audit does not read R1's row, so it is a consistency check a human might notice, not an input any script consumes.

WHY MEDIUM IS UNSUPPORTABLE: under §5, load_bearing == HIGH is criterion 1. MEDIUM and LOW produce the identical outcome (excluded), and R1 is independently excluded by criterion 3 via B1. R1 is excluded twice over by facts fixed before this audit began. Grading it MEDIUM implies a consequence that does not exist. Per G7 in the reverse direction: a classification must not be held above what the pipeline actually does with it merely because the row was interesting to write.

CONCRETE NAMED DEPENDENCY, stated plainly as the task requires: NONE that is computed. The only artifacts that consume R1 are results/T1_evidence_audit.tsv (one row, via scripts/build_tables.py) and the §1/§5 claim-count arithmetic in docs/DECISIONS.md.
adv.better_primary_source:
YES — the designated primary is the wrong paper for the claim as worded, though it is the right paper to have read.

TRUE ORIGINATING PRIMARY FOR THE IL-15 HALF: Verma S, Hiby SE, Loke YW, King A. "Human decidual natural killer cells express the receptor for and respond to the cytokine interleukin 15." Biol Reprod 2000;62(4):959-968. PMID 10727265, doi 10.1095/biolreprod62.4.959. Kopcow does not claim the experiment as his own — Results verbatim: "dNK cytotoxic capacity was regained upon incubation of the cells with IL-15 for 12 h (data not shown) or 36 h (Fig. 1B) AS DESCRIBED (15)", where ref 15 is Verma 2000. Kopcow's own contribution is n=3 with a single representative figure and no medium-only arm; Verma is where "IL-15 augments dNK cytolytic activity against K562" originates. The prior row named Verma but then designated Kopcow as "PRIMARY" — that is a retrievability decision presented as a provenance one, and the row should say so.

RETRIEVAL STATUS OF VERMA 2000 — searched thoroughly, could not obtain (explicitly NOT "did not search"): Europe PMC REST reports inEPMC=N, hasPDF=N, no PMCID; Unpaywall reports is_oa=true / oa_status=bronze with a single publisher-hosted location; that OUP PDF URL returns HTTP 403 to curl; www.biolreprod.org/content/62/4/959.full.pdf returns HTTP 200 HTML and 301-redirects to a journal index with no article; the OUP landing page (article/62/4/959/2734743) via WebFetch shows abstract only behind a EUR 39 paywall; a WebSearch for a mirror found none. ONE ROUTE INCOMPLETE: the archive.org Wayback availability API returned HTTP 429 and I did not retry — that specific route is NOT_SEARCHED-to-completion and is the obvious next attempt. Consequence under G1: Verma 2000 remains abstract+MeSH only and CANNOT carry a methods-derived classification. This is exactly why Kopcow, whose methods I did read in full, must remain the classification-bearing source even though Verma is the provenance-bearing one — and the row should state that split rather than collapsing it.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND BOOKKEEPING: Verma 2000's MeSH record carries substance terms for Interleukin-15, Interleukin-18 and Interleukin-12, with the qualifier headings "Interleukin-12 biosynthesis pharmacology" and "Interleukin-18 pharmacology" — indexing assigned from full text, indicating those agents were administered in that study. If so, the claim's "IL-15/IL-18" compound may originate in Verma 2000 itself, not in a downstream review as the prior row asserted. That is a lead, not a finding, and cannot be upgraded without the full text.

NO ADEQUATE PRIMARY EXISTS FOR THE IL-18 HALF. The only primary that tested IL-18 on decidual cells, Tokmadzic 2002 (PMID 12516629), reports the exact pair in the claim FAILING ("IL-18 combined with IL-10 or IL-15 did not show this effect"), with IL-12 as the working partner, and measured bulk decidual lymphocytes rather than purified dNK. Full text closed (Wiley), abstract only.

BETTER PRIMARIES FOR THE UNDERLYING QUESTION ("is fresh dNK effector function cytokine-restorable"), both retrievable and both with donor-level n, which Kopcow lacks: (i) PMID 41808348 / PMC12975338, Immunohorizons 2026 — OA FULL TEXT, fresh uncryopreserved cells, IL-12+IL-15+IL-18 each at 1 nM for 24 h, n = 6 blood / 8 DPI / 6 decidua from 6 MATCHED donors, the only donor-matched-compartment design in this literature; (ii) de Mendonca Vieira 2020, PMID 32376646 / PMC7322730, J Immunol, from Kopcow's own lab, term vs first-trimester dNK degranulation without any cytokine added. Neither is a lineage study and neither should be promoted as one.
